BREAKING — Adriana Raquel Canales was arrested Tuesday evening, October 20, 2026, at 8:43 p.m., by the Laredo Police Department on two third-degree felony charges, according to Webb County booking records.

Canales was booked into the Webb County Jail on (1) tampering with or fabricating physical evidence with intent to impair (charge code TAMPER/FABRICATE PHYS EVID W/INTENT TO IMPAIR) — a third-degree felony under Texas law, and (2) possession of a controlled substance, Penalty Group 2, 1 gram to under 4 grams — also a third-degree felony. Bond had not been set on either charge as of the booking record reviewed by Webb Watch 956. The Webb County public-access court records also flagged an active warrant indicator on her record.

The tampering charge alleges that physical evidence was altered or fabricated with intent to impair its availability as evidence; the drug charge alleges she possessed a Penalty Group 2 substance, which includes synthetic drugs such as THC extracts and certain synthetic cannabinoids and stimulants.

A third-degree felony in Texas is punishable by 2 to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000. Webb Watch 956 will follow this case as it moves through the Webb County courts.

An arrest is an allegation, not a conviction. Adriana Raquel Canales is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

Sources: Webb County Sheriff's Office Booking Jail Search (Oct. 20, 2026); Webb County public-access court records, Tyler Odyssey portal.

title: BREAKING: Adriana Canales Arrested on Felony Evidence-Tampering and Drug Charges
